meta.audience: The Gentiles and the house of Israel
meta.unit: The sealed record and the condition on it (Ether 4)
principles: A record with a release date written into it
A seal handed over with its own key
A test set on what a thing moves men to do

world_behind.title: A king held these writings for six hundred years' worth of the record
world_behind.text: Verse 1 says king Mosiah held them back until after Christ should show himself to his people. Mosiah 8:9 has the twenty-four plates brought to him, Mosiah 28:11 has him translate them, and Mosiah 28:20 has him hand everything to Alma.

world_behind.title: The release is dated by 3 Nephi
world_behind.text: Verse 2 puts it after Christ had truly showed himself to his people. 3 Nephi 26:6 to 11 reports what happened to the teaching of that visit: Mormon began to write it all and was forbidden, so the same restriction ran in both directions.

world_behind.title: They are going back into the ground
world_behind.text: Verse 3 has Moroni commanded to hide them up again in the earth, because all had dwindled in unbelief and the Lamanites had rejected the gospel. Ether 15:33 has Ether himself hiding his record in a manner the people of Limhi later found, so the same writings are buried twice by two men a thousand years apart.

world_behind.title: The interpreters were sealed with the writing
world_behind.text: Verse 5 says he sealed up the interpretation as well. Ether 3:23 to 28 has the two stones given to the brother of Jared for exactly this purpose, and Mosiah 28:13 describes them fastened into the rims of a bow.

world_behind.title: Ether 5:1 makes the seal a standing instruction
world_behind.text: The next chapter tells whoever receives the plates to touch the sealed part not, in order to translate. The prohibition is addressed forward, past Moroni, to a translator he never met.

world_behind.title: The speaker changes at verse 6
world_behind.text: From there to the end the Lord speaks in the first person, and Moroni does not resume. A chapter that begins as a record-keeping note becomes a direct address to the Gentiles without a seam.

words.text: To waste away by degrees. The record uses the word eleven times, always of a people losing belief, and the King James Bible not at all.
The two stones prepared for translating. Treated at Mosiah 8:13. It appears six times in the record, with none in the King James Bible.
To strive or dispute against. The record uses the word forty-four times and the King James Bible fourteen. Verse 8 pairs contending against the word with denying these things.
Moves a person toward something by argument or appeal. The word turns up six times, twice inside this chapter, here, and the King James Bible twice. Verse 12 makes it the test of what comes from God.
To tear apart with force. The record uses the word eight times and the King James Bible nineteen. Verse 15 applies it to a veil of unbelief.
Inability to see. Its count is eleven times in this book, while the King James Bible seven. Verse 15 attaches it to the mind rather than the eyes.
Opened out so the whole can be seen. The record uses the word four times and never the King James Bible. Verse 7 uses the related form of all the Lord's revelations.

phrases.term: Write the things which he had seen
phrases.text: The command that produced the sealed portion. The vision of chapter 3 became a document.

phrases.term: Until after that he should be lifted up upon the cross
phrases.text: The date set on the writing's release. The clock runs on an event.

phrases.term: For this cause did king Mosiah keep them
phrases.text: Moroni's account of why the plates sat in a king's custody. The holding was obedience to the same command.

phrases.term: They have all dwindled in unbelief
phrases.text: The reason given for hiding the record again. Verse 3 makes the loss of belief the deciding fact.

phrases.term: There never were greater things made manifest
phrases.text: Moroni's estimate of what he is sealing. He says it twice in one sentence.

phrases.term: Wherefore I have sealed up the interpreters
phrases.text: The seal and the means of opening it are stored together. Ether 3:23 gave him the two stones for this purpose.

phrases.term: Even as the brother of Jared did
phrases.text: The measure set on the Gentiles. Chapter 3 supplied the example this verse points back to.

phrases.term: For I am he who speaketh
phrases.text: The claim behind the warning. The sentence rests the whole chapter on who is talking.

phrases.term: For it persuadeth men to do good
phrases.text: The Spirit's witness described by its effect. Verse 12 turns this into a general rule.

phrases.term: The knowledge which is hid up because of unbelief
phrases.text: The cause named for the withholding. The lock is placed on the hearer's side.
An action asked of the reader. Chapter 3 had a veil taken away from a man; this one is torn by those behind it.

verses.label: v. 1–3
verses.title: Held, shown, hidden
verses.text: The Lord commands the brother of Jared to go down out of the mount from his presence and write what he had seen. Those writings were forbidden to come to the children of men until after Christ should be lifted up upon the cross, and for that reason king Mosiah kept them, so they would not come to the world until Christ had shown himself to his people. After Christ truly had showed himself, he commanded that they be made manifest. Since then all have dwindled in unbelief, none are left save the Lamanites, and they have rejected the gospel of Christ, so Moroni is commanded to hide the writings up again in the earth.

verses.label: v. 4–6
verses.title: Sealed with the key inside
verses.text: Moroni says he has written upon these plates the very things the brother of Jared saw, and that no greater things were ever made manifest than those. The Lord commanded him to write them and he has written them, commanded him to seal them up, and commanded him to seal up the interpretation as well, so he has sealed up the interpreters according to that commandment. The Lord told him the writings will not go forth to the Gentiles until the day they repent of their iniquity and become clean before the Lord.

verses.label: v. 7–9
verses.title: The condition and the warning
verses.text: In the day the Gentiles exercise faith in the Lord, even as the brother of Jared did, so they may become sanctified in him, he will manifest to them what the brother of Jared saw, unfolding all his revelations to them. The speaker names himself Jesus Christ, the Son of God, the Father of the heavens and of the earth and of all things in them. Whoever contends against the word of the Lord is accursed, and whoever denies these things is accursed, and to such no greater things will be shown, since he himself is the one speaking. At his command the heavens open and shut, at his word the earth shakes, and at his command the inhabitants of the earth pass away as by fire.

verses.label: v. 10–12
verses.title: The test of the words
verses.text: Whoever does not believe his words does not believe his disciples. If he is not the one speaking, the hearer may judge, and will know at the last day who was speaking. The one who believes what he has spoken will be visited with the manifestations of his Spirit and will know and bear record, since by that Spirit he will know these things are true, for it persuades men to do good. Whatever persuades men to do good is of him, since good comes of none other, and he is the same one who leads men to all good. Whoever will not believe his words will not believe him, and whoever will not believe him will not believe the Father who sent him. He is the Father, the light, the life, and the truth of the world.

verses.label: v. 13–15
verses.title: Two invitations
verses.text: The record issues the same invitation twice with the addressee changed and the diagnosis kept: "Come unto me, O ye Gentiles" at verse 13 and "Come unto me, O ye house of Israel" at verse 14. Both verses end on the same word, "because of unbelief," so the obstacle named for the outsiders and for the covenant people is identical. Verse 15 then gives the condition as an action on a physical object, "when ye shall rend that veil of unbelief," and supplies three things the veil sustains, wickedness, hardness of heart, and blindness of mind. The phrase "a broken heart and a contrite spirit" comes from Psalm 51:17 and is used at 3 Nephi 9:20 as the sacrifice that replaces burnt offerings.

verses.label: v. 16–17
verses.title: The sign
verses.text: The record names a New Testament writer and a New Testament book as things still sealed: "my revelations which I have caused to be written by my servant John be unfolded in the eyes of all the people." John is named this way twice in these books, here and at 1 Nephi 14:19–27, where an angel identifies the man who will write the vision Nephi is forbidden to record. Verse 17 then makes the volume in the reader's hands the sign, "when ye shall receive this record ye may know that the work of the Father has commenced." A book supplies its own arrival as the evidence for a claim about timing, which is a prediction that can be dated once the book exists.

verses.label: v. 18–19
verses.title: The terms
verses.text: He calls all the ends of the earth to repent, come to him, believe in his gospel, and be baptized in his name. Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, whoever believes not will be damned, and signs will follow them that believe in his name. Blessed is he that is found faithful to his name at the last day, for he will be lifted up to dwell in the kingdom prepared for him from the foundation of the world. Moroni closes with the Lord saying it is he that has spoken it.

chapter.title: The record carries its own release date
chapter.text: Verse 1 forbids it until after the cross and verse 2 releases it once Christ has appeared. The timing sits inside the text.

chapter.title: The seal was handed over with its key
chapter.text: Verse 5 has the interpretation sealed alongside the writing, using the stones given in Ether 3:23.

chapter.title: Unbelief is what closes the record
chapter.text: Verse 3 gives dwindling as the reason for hiding it, and verse 13 names unbelief as what the knowledge is hid behind.

chapter.title: The condition is measured against a person
chapter.text: Verse 7 sets the standard at the faith the brother of Jared showed. Chapter 3 recorded that faith so this verse could point back to it.

chapter.title: The speaker gives a test anyone can run
chapter.text: Verse 12 rests the judgment on what a thing moves a man toward. The test is on the effect.

chapter.title: Two invitations share one wording
chapter.text: Verses 13 and 14 both open with come unto me, addressed first to Gentiles and then to the house of Israel.

chapter.title: The veil has moved
chapter.text: Chapter 3 had a veil taken off the eyes of a man who believed; verse 15 asks those behind it to tear it themselves.

chapter.title: The chapter ends in ordinary terms
chapter.text: Verses 18 and 19 close a chapter about sealed visions with repentance, baptism, and remaining faithful.

applications.title: Putting something away can be the assignment
applications.text: Moroni reports that with everyone dwindled into unbelief he was commanded to hide the record up again in the earth. Not every faithful act with a good thing is publication, and this one is a deliberate withdrawal.

applications.title: Do the part that is not sealed
applications.text: The condition given is repentance and cleanness. Nothing in it requires access to hidden pages.

applications.title: The standard is named as a person
applications.text: The condition for the greater things is that they exercise faith even as the brother of Jared did. A standard set by an example rather than a threshold is easier to picture and much harder to game.

applications.title: He puts the question back to the reader
applications.text: "If it so be that I do not speak, judge ye" leaves the assessment with the hearer and names the day it gets settled. Confidence that invites a verdict is a different thing from confidence that forbids one.

applications.title: Judge a thing by what it moves you to do
applications.text: The test offered is whether it persuades men to do good. That can be applied today.

applications.title: Name your own unbelief
applications.text: The knowledge is described as hid up because of unbelief. Locating the unbelief is the first move.

applications.title: Come with a broken heart
applications.text: The verse pairs rending the veil with calling on the Father in that manner. Both are asked at once.

applications.title: Receiving it is itself the news
applications.text: When you receive this record, the verse says, you may know that the work of the Father has commenced upon all the face of the land. The arrival is the announcement, so there is nothing further to wait for.

questions.text: Where have I dwindled slowly enough not to notice?
What has been kept back from me for a reason I never asked about?
Am I clean in the sense this verse gives?
Whose faith would I be measured against?
Have I contended against something I had not read?
What persuades me to do good, and do I trust it?
What veil of unbelief am I holding in place?
